_what: Binaries in the installer payload permitted to contain the build account name. Consumed by tools/gate/check_package_account_name.py (GitHub #199 / #191).
_it_is_empty_and_that_is_the_point: Zero entries, so the guard enforces zero rather than a tolerated count. Measured 2026-09-30 over the REAL install population -- cmake --install, which runs the _required_dlls rules and windeployqt: 63 binaries listed, 63 read, 0 occurrences, with this allowlist empty. All 418 occurrences GitHub #199 enumerated are gone from the packaged artifact set.
_how_zero_was_reached: Three mechanisms, in this order of preference. (1) PDFE-owned sources fixed outright: RUSTFLAGS=--remap-path-prefix removed 285 cargo file!() paths and OPENSSL_NO_FILENAMES removed 6 OPENSSL_FILE paths, taking pdfe.exe 291 -> 0. (2) Third-party dependency DLLs rebuilt through a neutral build root (scripts/Set-NeutralBuildRoot.ps1): tesseract55 106 -> 0, libcrypto 16 -> 0, libssl 2 -> 0, tiff 1 -> 0. Each checked for vacuity, because 0 cannot distinguish 'gone' from 're-rooted' -- tesseract55.dll still holds exactly 106 embedded source paths, re-rooted rather than absent. (3) What neither could reach -- Qt6Widgets.dll's 2 paths, because qtbase cannot be rebuilt on that host (#272) -- is removed by the post-build scrub, tools/gate/scrub_package_account_name.py, wired into windows-validation.yml between the Release build and cpack. See docs/audit/dca/0111-the-guard-population-never-included-what-shipped.md.
_an_entry_here_was_tried_and_withdrawn: An earlier revision carried bin/Qt6Widgets.dll with max: 2 and a written reason. The validator gate FAILED the phase for it, correctly: criteria 1 and 3 say 0 occurrences without qualification, and a capped allowlist entry is a tolerated leak rather than a fix. The post-build scrub -- which criterion 1 names explicitly, alongside build-path stripping and deterministic build flags -- closes it properly, so the entry is gone. Recorded because the next person facing an awkward residual will reach for this file first, and the gate will not accept it.
_absent_file_fails_closed: load_allowlist() returns an empty mapping when this file is missing, so deleting it permits nothing rather than everything. The file exists to record the decision, not to enable it.
_before_adding_an_entry: An entry here concedes that a shipped binary discloses the build account name to every user who runs strings on it. Exhaust the three mechanisms above first -- in particular the scrub, which needs no rebuild and is verified to preserve byte length, the export table and loadability. If an entry is genuinely unavoidable (a port shipping prebuilt binaries that is ALSO signed, so neither a rebuild nor the scrub can touch it) give it a 'max' cap so any INCREASE still reddens, and state the reason. An uncapped entry is a permanent blind spot: the count could go from 1 to 10,000 and this guard would keep passing.
_entry_format: "bin/some.dll": {"max": 3, "reason": "why neither a rebuild nor the scrub can reach this"}  -- the key is the path relative to the scan root, forward slashes.
